title: Local Money Bought the Bounce. Foreign Money Sold It.
deck: IHSG rose 4.90% to 5,439.258 while foreign investors sold a net Rp6.67tn, more than twice the week before. Buyback plans and a state fund that says it is buying point to local support, though nobody has reported how much was spent. The rally won back 28% of last week's loss. It has not yet shown that foreign investors are willing to return.

sections.title: A rally we would not chase yet

blocks.text: IHSG rose 4.90% to 5,439.258. It won back 254.153 of the 908.654 points lost the week before, about 28%. The index is still 10.74% below its 9 October close and would need to rise 12.03% to get there.

Who bought matters more than how far prices went. Foreign investors sold a net Rp6.67tn across all stock markets, more than twice the previous week's Rp3.19tn. Local buyers took all of it and still pushed prices up. We know less about who those buyers were. Several listed companies filed plans to buy back their own shares, the four Barito group companies alone up to Rp3.5tn, but none has yet reported what it bought. Danantara, the state investment fund, says it started buying state-owned stocks on 21 October and has given no amounts. So the support is announced capacity and stated intent. How much of the rally it paid for is not yet known.

Our view stays defensive. A rally carried by local buyers against foreign sellers, with issuers and a state fund promising more, has not shown that outside investors trust the market again. We would change our mind when foreign selling in the largest banks stops, and when the index change on 2 November produces a cleaner IHSG that holds its gains.

blocks.label: Checking last week's call
blocks.text: Last week our planning case put IHSG between 4,437 and 5,185 over four to twelve weeks. Monday's low of 4,907 sat inside that range. Friday's close of 5,439 sat above it, 0.89% short of the 5,488 where our relief case began. The bounce came faster than we planned for. None of the conditions we attached to the relief case has been met, though IDX announced steps toward two of them. We keep the planning case and say plainly that the first week went against it.

blocks.label: Exhibit 01
blocks.title: A fall on Monday, then four higher closes
blocks.note: Select a date to inspect the closing observation. Lines join daily closes and show no intraday highs or lows.

event.label: IDX said HSC stocks will leave IHSG

blocks.text: Monday was the first session under IDX's new 7% lower price limit. IHSG fell 3.64% to 4,996.609 and touched 4,907.370 during the day, 5.36% below the previous Friday. BBCA fell 6.86% to Rp4,820, its new lower limit.

Two statements came on Monday. IDX president director Jeffrey Hendrik said every high shareholding concentration (HSC) stock would be taken out of IHSG, about 18% of the index by his estimate. Danantara's chief operating officer, Dony Oskaria, said the fund would add to its holdings of state-owned companies with strong fundamentals. Before Monday's open, the four Barito group companies, BRPT, BREN, TPIA and CUAN, had filed buyback plans with IDX worth up to Rp3.5tn together. They rely on OJK's rules for a significantly fluctuating market.

On Tuesday IHSG rose 5.65% and closed at its high of 5,278.888. The state-owned names did most of the lifting. TLKM rose 16.38%, BBRI 9.84% and BMRI 9.82%. Foreign investors still sold a net Rp2.19tn that day. Danantara was probably not Tuesday's buyer. On 22 October its chief investment officer, Pandu Sjahrir, said the fund had started buying "per kemarin, hari ini", as of the day before and that day. He named no stocks and no amounts. Tuesday's buying came from other local investors, possibly including companies with fresh buyback plans. The data cannot tell them apart.

The rest of the week rose by less than 1.2% a day. Thursday opened with a sharp drop to 5,185.527 at 09:01, 2.68% below Wednesday's close, and climbed back by midday. We found no official explanation for it.
Trading was heavier. Regular-market value averaged Rp18.02tn a day, 33.7% more than the week before, and Tuesday alone saw Rp25.25tn. Negotiated trades made up 11.38% of all stock value.

By count the rise was broad. 651 stocks rose and 155 fell. By value it was narrower. Stocks worth Rp2,921tn fell, 30.66% of the value in IDX's chart. IDX again printed the two falling groups' percentages in the wrong order, in both bars. We recompute every share from the counts.

sections.title: Foreign investors sold into the rise

blocks.label: Exhibit 02
blocks.title: Net selling on four of five days
blocks.note: Official all-market stock trading, foreign purchases less sales. This measures trading, not money leaving the country.

blocks.text: Wednesday was the only day of foreign net buying, and only Rp12.49bn. The week's net selling of Rp6.67tn was 108.83% more than the week before. Foreign net selling this year has reached Rp94.87tn, and this week added 7.03% of it. Foreign investors still made up 40% of trading, the same share as the week before. They kept trading and they kept selling.

blocks.caption: Each explanation tested against the evidence that would rule it out

blocks.text: We tested each explanation against the evidence most likely to rule it out. Two fail outright. Foreigners did not return, and the rest of Asia mostly fell. The explanation that survives is local buying of large caps, with issuers and the state fund announcing support. It has the weakness that matters most. Nobody has said how much was actually spent.

Our stock-level estimate covers the 87 liquid large caps with at least Rp10tn of market value and Rp10bn of average daily trading. It puts their regular-market foreign net selling at Rp8.13tn. The estimate values foreign share volume at each day's close and leaves out negotiated trades, so it measures something different from IDX's official total. We use it only to see which stocks foreigners sold.

sections.title: State banks rose. Foreigners sold them anyway.

blocks.label: Exhibit 03
blocks.title: Six leaders and four laggards
blocks.note: Official weekly IHSG contributions from IDX. The ten largest gainers added 199.84 points in all.

blocks.text: Four state-owned stocks, BMRI, BBRI, TLKM and BBNI, added 126.51 points. That is 49.78% of the week's 254.153-point gain. The ten largest contributors added 199.84 points, or 78.63%. LQ45 rose 7.57% and IDX BUMN20 rose 12.84%, both well ahead of IHSG.

Foreigners were net sellers of every stock in this table. They still bought an estimated Rp2,298.85bn of BBRI, but sold Rp4,463.88bn, a net Rp2.17tn, while the price rose 10.23%. Local buyers set that price. Foreign money gave the rise no net support, and nothing in the week tells us how much it would absorb if local demand faded.

BBCA shows the other side of the same trade. It was the most traded stock on the exchange, 15.14% of all stock value according to IDX, and it fell 2.90% while its own buyback was reported to be running. Its estimated foreign net selling of Rp2.95tn was the largest of any stock. Our reading is that funds cutting Indonesia sell first where they can sell in size, and BBCA is where they can. On that reading the fall says more about liquidity than about the bank. The other possibility is that foreigners are cutting BBCA on its own merits. One week of data cannot tell the two apart.

sections.title: Too many index points come from stocks that barely trade

blocks.text: IDX has now acted on the problem MSCI raised. On 22 October it confirmed that IHSG will drop HSC stocks from Monday 2 November. The capped free-float method stays. A stock newly placed on the HSC list will leave IHSG at once, without waiting for a review, and one taken off the list becomes eligible for the index again. IDX and KSEI decide the list together. A list of 80 stocks published on 19 October includes DCII, BYAN, BREN, DSSA and MORA.

rows: Share of regular trading this week
blocks.caption: Our calculation from daily closes and shares outstanding, using the 19 October list. Changes are weighted by full market value, not by IHSG weight

blocks.text: That is the problem in two numbers. These 80 companies are 28% of what the market is said to be worth and 3% of what actually changes hands. Their prices can move the index with very little money behind them. MORA fell 6.91%, 6.87%, 6.19% and 6.92% on four straight days, near the new 7% limit, then rose 9.46% on Friday. It traded Rp6.12bn all week and took 11.67 points off IHSG. BBRI needed Rp9,188bn of trading to add 39.76 points. For each rupiah traded, MORA moved the index about 440 times as far as BBRI.

DCII is worth Rp431tn at its last price. It traded Rp1.24bn in five days and had two sessions with no trades at all in the past 20. It still cost the index 7.32 points. BREN went the other way. It rose 28.3% and added 20.39 points on Rp379.91bn of trading, in the week it filed a buyback plan of up to Rp1tn. How much BREN actually bought has not been reported.

blocks.label: Our assessment
blocks.text: Removing these stocks will make IHSG a more honest measure of prices investors can actually trade. It changes no company's value. It does change what the headline number measures, so IHSG after 2 November will not compare directly with IHSG today. A gain built partly on thin, concentrated stocks will become harder to produce.

sections.title: Every sector rose. Technology stayed flat.

blocks.label: Exhibit 04
blocks.title: Sector index changes over the week
blocks.note: Weekly price changes of the IDX sector indices.

blocks.text: Transport and logistics rose most, by 9.02%. Energy gained 6.37% and infrastructure 5.68%. Technology rose only 0.03%. DCII, by far its largest company by market value, fell 3.81%. The Main Board index rose 6.26%. The Development Board rose 0.87% and the Acceleration Board 1.08%. The larger and more liquid the stock, the better it did, which is what we would expect when the main buyers are defending large stocks.

The authorities moved quickly. On 20 October IDX set a Rp1 lower limit for shares priced Rp11 to Rp14 on the Main, Development and New Economy boards. On 21 October Bank Indonesia held the BI-Rate at 5.75%, raised its Deposit Facility rate to 5.00% and cut conventional banks' reserve requirement from 9% to 7%, in steps on 1 November and 1 December. On 22 October IDX confirmed the HSC change and moved its index reviews to January, April, July and October.

On 21 October OJK handed sanction letters to the parties it had fined. It puts capital-market fines up to 16 October at Rp2.52tn, made up of Rp2.23tn in case fines on 166 parties and Rp293.78bn in late-filing fines on 805 parties. The Rp2.1tn of fines linked to DSSA, BREN and CUAN is part of the first figure. OJK says criminal follow-up is possible if the evidence is sufficient. That is a possibility, not a case.

MSCI published nothing new that we could find. IDX says it met MSCI representatives before announcing the HSC change. The consultation on moving Indonesia to standalone status runs to 30 April 2027, with a decision due by 30 June 2027.

blocks.label: Our assessment
blocks.text: The direction is right. Dropping HSC stocks and marking whether large shareholders are affiliated both answer MSCI's complaint about hidden ownership. For now they are announcements. The test is whether the shareholder data that comes out of them lets an outsider work out who controls a company's shares.

blocks.caption: Last week's tests for a durable recovery

blocks.title: The rupiah barely moved
blocks.note: The starting values use this week's IHSG and BI JISDOR. Move the sliders to try a different currency assumption. The equity close and the reference rate are taken at different times.

blocks.text: JISDOR went from Rp18,052 to Rp18,069 per dollar, a 0.09% rise. The rough dollar return on IHSG was 4.80% before costs and hedging. The currency neither added to the gain nor took much away.

From 26 to 30 October we will watch whether foreign selling in BBRI and BBCA slows, and for any report of what Danantara and the buyback programmes actually spent. Then, on 2 November, comes the first IHSG without HSC stocks. Our relief case begins at 5,488, 0.89% above Friday's close. A close above it on its own will not change our view. A close above it with foreign buying would.

blocks.label: Investment conclusion
blocks.text: Local money can carry prices for a while, and this week it did. We stay cautious on a broad recovery until foreign investors stop selling the stocks they can sell most easily. Traders can use the bounce. Investors still need the ownership and enforcement evidence we set out last week.

method: Official foreign trading totals cover all stock markets. Stock-level foreign values are regular-market estimates from foreign share volumes valued at daily closes, for stocks with at least Rp10tn market value and Rp10bn 20-session average daily value. Daily regular-market value and volume in the estimates match all five IDX daily reports exactly. HSC group figures use the 80-stock list published on 19 October, shares outstanding and daily closes, weighted by full market value: sum of shares times close on the later date over the same sum on the earlier date, less one. They are not IHSG weights. Every input is frozen in the HSC comparison file. Breadth shares are recomputed from counts. Index contributions and sector changes are read from rendered IDX pages.
displayMethod: Price returns exclude dividends and costs. Dollar returns use JISDOR and are indicative. Official all-market flows and regular-market stock estimates have different scopes. Exact observations and calculations are available beside the exhibits and in the linked snapshots.
